Be good if you revisited the r1. They have delivered everything they promised and I've been using web agents it introduced a few months back to automate all sorts of things. All for free of course. The advantages of a curated AI service is they bolt in and can swap out AI's for better ones as they develop. And they are. Some of the extra things they didn't announce but have been there for months. Gen Voice.. You can set the voice with a text or voice prompt. Gen UI.. You can set the UI with a voice/text or photo prompt. Can your smartphone Ai change it's out put o be a 70's text terminal with animated glitchy vector fonts and screen wobble? :-) It's become far more robust, mixing in the advanced beta rabbit function into all interactions. Been able to submit my time-sheets, check latest emails, add to calendar all via agents is a treat. Yes, some things can be a bit janky initially, but what AI isn't? Apple has been forced to shut down part of it's AI offering, way to janky! ;-) Agents are a HUGE thing for elderly and disabled. Who apart from Rabbit Tech has agents right now in a device that can be used by those that can't operate a smartphone? It's been rather useful to ask it "list the closest bushfire to me and tell me in the next 3 days are the winds expects to blow from the bushfire area toward my home"... Got a perfect response with all the details I needed and a short summary! As I work with people of various abilities I can confirm the Rabbit r1, with it's design and colour, generates a vibe of fun and experimentation on a device I can happily had around. If I try the same with a smartphone it's produces a vastly different vibe.. more one of suspicion. I also like the fact you can influence the company and make suggestions they actually read ;-) You are far less an 'invisible' user as you are with Google, FB, Apple etc etc.
